/-!
# Open coloring axiom

The open coloring axiom (OCA) is an axiom about colorings of the pairs of a set of reals.
Two versions were introduced, by Abraham, Rubin and Shelah [ARS85] and by Todorčević [To89].
The version spelled out in the Wikipedia article, and formalized here, is Todorčević's.

**Todorčević's open coloring axiom.** Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and color each pair of
distinct elements of $X$ either white or black, so that the set of white pairs is open in
$X \times X$. Then either
- $X$ has an uncountable subset all of whose pairs are white, or
- $X$ is the union of countably many subsets, each of which has all of its pairs black.

Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems asks: *Is OCA (the open coloring axiom) consistent with
$2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$?* Todorčević's OCA implies that the bounding number $\mathfrak{b}$
equals $\aleph_2$, hence $2^{\aleph_0} \geq \aleph_2$; it is open whether the continuum can be
strictly larger than $\aleph_2$ in a model of OCA. (For the Abraham–Rubin–Shelah version the
analogous question was answered positively by Gilton and Neeman [GN22].)

## Formalization notes

- **Colorings as graphs.** A black/white coloring of the pairs of $X$ is recorded as a
  `SimpleGraph X` whose edges are the white pairs. White-homogeneous sets are cliques
  (`SimpleGraph.IsClique`) and black-homogeneous sets are independent sets
  (`SimpleGraph.IsIndepSet`). The openness hypothesis is that the adjacency relation is an open
  subset of `X × X`, where `X` carries the subspace topology of `ℝ`. Since the diagonal is closed
  in `X × X`, this is the same as openness of the set of white pairs in the complete graph on `X`.
- **Countable partitions.** "A partition of $X$ into countably many black-homogeneous sets" is
  recorded as a cover of $X$ by an `ℕ`-indexed family of independent sets. This is equivalent:
  a subset of an independent set is independent, so any such cover can be refined to a partition,
  and a finite or countable family can be re-indexed by `ℕ` (repeating sets or using `∅`).
- **Consistency placeholder.** The question is a *relative consistency* question
  (does $\mathrm{ZFC} + \mathrm{OCA} + 2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$ have a model?). Lean works inside
  one fixed model of its set theory and Mathlib has no syntactic first-order theory of ZFC, so
  this cannot be expressed directly. Following the convention used elsewhere in this repository
  (e.g. `Erdos1175.erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`), the problem is recorded as an
  `answer(sorry)` placeholder equivalent to the conjunction `OCA ∧ ℵ₂ < 𝔠`; the intended
  mathematical content is the model-theoretic statement
  $\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}) \to
  \mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC} + \mathrm{OCA} + 2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2)$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Open coloring axiom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/open_coloring_axiom)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [ARS85] Abraham, U., Rubin, M., Shelah, S., *On the consistency of some partition theorems for
  continuous colorings, and the structure of ℵ₁-dense real order types*,
  Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 29 (1985), 123–206.
- [To89] Todorčević, S., [*Partition problems in topology*](https://archive.org/details/partitionproblem0000todo),
  Contemporary Mathematics 84, American Mathematical Society (1989).
- [Mo10] Moore, J. T., [*The proper forcing axiom*](https://www.math.cornell.edu/~justin/Ftp/ICM.pdf),
  Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM 2010), Vol. II, 3–29.
- [GN22] Gilton, T., Neeman, I., *Abraham–Rubin–Shelah open colorings and a large continuum*,
  J. Math. Log. 22 (2022).
-/

def OCA : Prop :=
  ∀ (X : Set ℝ) (G : SimpleGraph X), IsOpen {p : X × X | G.Adj p.1 p.2} →
    (∃ Y : Set X, ¬ Y.Countable ∧ G.IsClique Y) ∨

blocks.docstring:
**Todorčević's open coloring axiom** (OCA).

For every set of reals $X$ and every coloring of the pairs of distinct elements of $X$ in black
and white such that the set of white pairs is open in $X \times X$, either
- there is an uncountable $Y \subseteq X$ all of whose pairs are white, or
- $X$ is a countable union of sets all of whose pairs are black.

The coloring is recorded as a graph `G : SimpleGraph X` whose edges are the white pairs, so the
openness hypothesis says that `{p : X × X | G.Adj p.1 p.2}` is open in `X × X`,
white-homogeneous sets are cliques of `G`, and black-homogeneous sets are independent sets of `G`.

blocks.name: OCA
blocks.text:
/--
**Todorčević's open coloring axiom** (OCA).

For every set of reals $X$ and every coloring of the pairs of distinct elements of $X$ in black
and white such that the set of white pairs is open in $X \times X$, either
- there is an uncountable $Y \subseteq X$ all of whose pairs are white, or
- $X$ is a countable union of sets all of whose pairs are black.

The coloring is recorded as a graph `G : SimpleGraph X` whose edges are the white pairs, so the
openness hypothesis says that `{p : X × X | G.Adj p.1 p.2}` is open in `X × X`,
white-homogeneous sets are cliques of `G`, and black-homogeneous sets are independent sets of `G`.
-/
def OCA : Prop :=
  ∀ (X : Set ℝ) (G : SimpleGraph X), IsOpen {p : X × X | G.Adj p.1 p.2} →
    (∃ Y : Set X, ¬ Y.Countable ∧ G.IsClique Y) ∨
    (∃ Y : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, G.IsIndepSet (Y n)) ∧ ⋃ n, Y n = Set.univ)

@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem open_coloring_axiom : answer(sorry) ↔ (OCA ∧ (ℵ_ 2 : Cardinal.{0}) < 𝔠) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Is OCA (the open coloring axiom) consistent with $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$?

Here OCA is Todorčević's open coloring axiom `OCA`, and `𝔠 = 2 ^ ℵ₀` is the cardinality of
the continuum, so `ℵ_ 2 < 𝔠` is the statement $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$. OCA implies
$\mathfrak{b} = \aleph_2$, so $\mathfrak{c} \geq \aleph_2$ in every model of OCA; the question
is whether the continuum can be strictly larger.

**Formalization caveat (consistency placeholder).** The question is a relative consistency
statement: it asks whether $\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC})$ implies
$\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC} + \mathrm{OCA} + 2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2)$. Lean works inside a single
fixed model of its set theory and has no syntactic first-order theory ZFC available, so
consistency cannot be expressed directly. Following the repository convention for such questions
(see `Erdos1175.erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`), the question is recorded as an
`answer(sorry)` placeholder for the proposition `OCA ∧ ℵ_ 2 < 𝔠` that a witnessing model must
satisfy: `answer(True)` corresponds to a positive answer ("yes, it is consistent") and
`answer(False)` to a negative one (OCA refutes $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$).

pairs `{(x, y) | x ≠ y}` is open in `X × X`. Hence the openness hypothesis of `OCA` is satisfied
by a coloring other than the all-black one.

@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem open_coloring_axiom.test.countable (X : Set ℝ) (hX : X.Countable) (G : SimpleGraph X) :
    ∃ Y : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, G.IsIndepSet (Y n)) ∧ ⋃ n, Y n = Set.univ := by
  rcases X.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hne
  · refine ⟨fun _ => ∅, fun _ => Set.pairwise_empty _, Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun x => ?_⟩
    exact absurd x.2 (Set.notMem_empty x.1)
  · have : Countable X := hX.to_subtype
    have : Nonempty X := hne.to_subtype
    obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := exists_surjective_nat X
    refine ⟨fun n => {f n}, fun n => Set.pairwise_singleton _ _,
      Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun x => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := hf x
    exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨n, Set.mem_singleton _⟩
blocks.docstring:
For a countable set of reals the second alternative of `OCA` holds for every coloring: the
set is a countable union of singletons, which are trivially black-homogeneous. Hence `OCA` is
only non-trivial for uncountable `X`.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (relative consistency over ZFC of OCA + ℵ₂ < 𝔠, i.e. Con(ZFC) → Con(ZFC + OCA + 2^{ℵ₀} > ℵ₂)); 'OCA' must be read as Todorčević's version, which is the one the article's Statement section actually spells out (for X ⊆ ℝ, equivalently any separable metric space, and a symmetric coloring whose white set is open in X × X: either an uncountable white-homogeneous subset exists or X is a countable union of black-homogeneous sets) and the one for which the question is open (OCA_T forces 𝔟 = ℵ₂, so the issue is whether 𝔠 can exceed ℵ₂; the Abraham–Rubin–Shelah version is known consistent with 𝔠 = ℵ₃ by Gilton–Neeman); since Lean works in a fixed model and Mathlib has no syntactic first-order ZFC theory, the repo precedent (Erdős 1175 shelah_consistency / 1119) is to record this as `answer(sorry) ↔ (OCA ∧ Cardinal.aleph 2 < Cardinal.continuum)` with a bespoke `OCA` Prop and an explicit consistency-placeholder caveat in the docstring.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the slot in the prescribed shape `answer(sorry) ↔ (OCA ∧ ℵ₂ < 𝔠)` with a faithful bespoke Todorčević-OCA Prop (X ⊆ ℝ, symmetric open white set in the product of subspace topologies, uncountable white clique ∨ countable cover by black-homogeneous sets). c07 is chosen as the base: its `SimpleGraph` encoding builds symmetry/irreflexivity in by construction (an arbitrary open relation would make the axiom refutable), uses idiomatic `IsClique`/`IsIndepSet`, pins the cardinal inequality to `Cardinal.{0}` (c01/c02/c05/c06 leave a free universe parameter, making the theorem needlessly universe-polymorphic), and includes a proved boundary-case test. I added c03's `⊤`-is-open test (openness hypothesis is satisfiable non-trivially) and tightened docstrings; the statement itself is c07's verbatim.

/-!

/--

items: Consistency placeholder: the question 'Is OCA consistent with 2^{ℵ₀} > ℵ₂?' is Con(ZFC) → Con(ZFC + OCA + ℵ₂ < 𝔠). Lean works in one fixed model and Mathlib has no syntactic ZFC theory, so (per the decomposition notes and repo precedent 1175/1119) the file states `answer(sorry) ↔ (OCA ∧ ℵ_ 2 < 𝔠)` and documents explicitly that the intended reading is the model-theoretic one and that `answer(True)` = 'yes, consistent'. A reviewer should confirm they accept this precedent-based encoding; read literally in Lean's model it asserts truth rather than consistency.

OCA is Todorčević's version (OCA_T), the one the Wikipedia article's Statement section spells out and the one for which the question is open (OCA_T forces 𝔟 = ℵ₂; the Abraham–Rubin–Shelah version is known to be consistent with 𝔠 = ℵ₃ by Gilton–Neeman). The ARS version is not formalized.

Domain of OCA: X ranges over `Set ℝ` (subsets of the reals), as in the Wikipedia Statement section, rather than over arbitrary separable metric spaces. The article states these are equivalent (a separable metric space embeds by a continuous injection into 2^ℕ ⊆ ℝ taking the open coloring to an open coloring). The universe is thereby fixed at 0.

Coloring encoded as `G : SimpleGraph X` whose edges are the white pairs; this builds in symmetry and irreflexivity of the coloring (the article's 'pairs' are unordered pairs of distinct elements). This matters: quantifying over arbitrary (non-symmetric) open relations on X × X would make the axiom refutable in ZFC (e.g. the relation `<`). Openness is `IsOpen {p : X × X | G.Adj p.1 p.2}` with the product of the subspace topologies from ℝ (verified via pp.explicit).
White-homogeneous = `G.IsClique Y` (Set.Pairwise G.Adj), black-homogeneous = `G.IsIndepSet Y` (Set.Pairwise ¬G.Adj). 'Uncountable subset' = `¬ Y.Countable`.

'Partitioned into a countable number of subsets' is encoded as a cover `⋃ n, Y n = Set.univ` by an ℕ-indexed family of independent sets. Equivalent to a partition into finitely or countably many black-homogeneous pieces: subsets of independent sets are independent (so a cover refines to a partition), and finite/countable families can be reindexed by ℕ using repeats or ∅.
`2^{ℵ₀} > ℵ₂` is rendered as `(ℵ_ 2 : Cardinal.{0}) < 𝔠` (Mathlib's `Cardinal.continuum = 2 ^ ℵ₀`), with the universe annotation to avoid an unassigned universe level.

Added one `@[category test]` theorem `OCA.test.countable` (with proof) checking that for countable X the second alternative of OCA holds for every coloring, as a basic API test for the bespoke definition.

Lean has a fixed model and Mathlib no syntactic ZFC theory, so — per the decomposition table and the existing repo precedent `Erdos1175.erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency` — the final file records it as an explicit `answer(sorry)` consistency placeholder with the caveat in both module and theorem docstrings. Read literally, `answer(True)` asserts truth of OCA ∧ ℵ₂ < 𝔠 in Lean's ambient model rather than consistency; `answer(False)` does correspond to the genuine negative answer (OCA ⊢ 𝔠 ≤ ℵ₂). Reviewers should be aware this is the accepted-precedent encoding, not a literal rendering; a human may prefer to reject consistency questions wholesale. 'OCA' is read as Todorčević's version (the one Wikipedia's Statement section spells out and the one for which the question is open; the ARS version is known consistent with 𝔠 = ℵ₃ by Gilton–Neeman). The subsets-of-ℝ formulation is equivalent to the separable-metric-space formulation (article states this). 'Partitioned into countably many' is encoded as an ℕ-indexed cover, equivalent because subsets of black-homogeneous sets are black-homogeneous. No candidate omitted or bailed; all compiled.
